beads.title: Closed loop: measure unattended quality against turn count
beads.body: The deliverable is the CURVE, not the artifacts. docs/CLOSED-LOOP.md is the design record; this graph is its execution. A programme that cannot report 'this does not work' is not an experiment — every phase below carries a stop-if.

beads.title: Ticket graph: append-only ledger with derived scheduling
beads.body: JSONL, last-record-per-id wins, so two branches merge by concatenation. Blocked-ness is derived, never stored. dead-end is a first-class kind: the memory that stops turn 30 redoing turn 4.

beads.title: Contagion firewall: assert a loop commit's blast radius
beads.body: CLOSED-LOOP.md 7 required this before the first autonomous commit. 140 of 151 workflows are push-triggered; the check asserts the set a loop commit can wake is a subset of the set it declares. Fails towards yes.

beads.title: loop.mino.mobi — the public viewing surface for the graph
beads.body: The apparatus is operator content, so it lives on mino.mobi. The artifacts a loop builds are agent-generated and belong on minomobi.com. CLOSED-LOOP.md 6.1.

beads.title: Phase 1 — pilot: one artifact, 10 turns, judge stubbed as a human-scored rubric
beads.body: STOP-IF: turns 5-10 are not visibly better than 1-4. That is a result, and the programme stops. The pilot exists to be cheap enough that a negative result is affordable. Second job: replace the cost estimate in CLOSED-LOOP.md 10, which is flagged there as the weakest number in the document.

beads.title: Phase 2 — the judge: probes + rubric + adversarial, calibrated against the pilot's human scores
beads.body: STOP-IF: the judge disagrees with people. There is no evaluation function anywhere in this repo today (CLOSED-LOOP.md 3, checked not assumed). A closed loop without a judge is a random walk with a commit log. Disagreement between the three signals is itself data.

beads.title: Phase 3 — seed the graph from the 59 BRIEF.md plan sections and the refusal reports
beads.body:
There is a second backlog nobody is reading: every lab site's BRIEF.md ends with a section its agent wrote FOR ITS SUCCESSOR. 59 of them, inert since the day each was written. That is a bead in all but name — state, ordering, a handoff — sitting as unqueryable prose on a published page.

DROPPED: Superseded by the greenfield decision (lp-DECISION below). The 59 BRIEF.md plan sections are community submissions — other people's projects, requested in their own threads. Spending 20-40 unattended turns iterating on them is a bad fit whoever benefits, and the backlog being convenient is not a reason. Greenfield replaces this phase: the operator writes a spec and a planner decomposes it.

beads.title: Phase 4 — the run: budgeted, instrumented, on its own surface
beads.body: 3-5 artifacts x 20-40 turns, not 100 x 1. Depth over breadth: the curve only exists along the turn axis, and breadth is the thing we already know. Stop conditions all three required.

beads.title: Phase 5 — publish the curve
beads.body: The deliverable. Most agent-loop demonstrations show you a terminal and ask you to be impressed; a measured quality-against-duration curve is a genuinely unusual public artifact.

beads.title: Flip .github/loop/config.json enabled to true
beads.body: The master switch, off by design. Same shape as ANNOUNCE in bsky-hello.yml and BOT_ENABLED in the factory: the expensive, irreversible half starts with a diff someone signed. Do not flip before Phase 1 has run attended at least once.

beads.title: Set CRON_GITHUB_PAT so the cron trampoline can dispatch the loop off-main
beads.body: workers/cron has never dispatched anything — GITHUB_PAT was never set and every fire is a silent 401. The loop needs it: GitHub runs schedule: only from the default branch, and the loop's state lives on a feature branch. Fine-grained PAT, this repo, Actions:write, nothing else.

beads.title: Which coupling shape? A shared world, a protocol, a compiler, or migrations over live data
beads.body: OPERATOR'S CALL (CLOSED-LOOP.md 11.1). This repo has 5 of the 7 characteristics of scale and is missing exactly the two that produce the feeling — irreducible coupling and an unholdable spec — ON PURPOSE. 60 of 80 surfaces depend on nothing. Reintroducing coupling is a real loss of a property currently enjoyed and should be spent knowingly.

beads.title: May the loop re-publish an existing site nobody asked it to touch?
beads.body:
OPERATOR'S CALL (CLOSED-LOOP.md 11.2). Instinct: yes where the plan was written in the requester's own thread and they saw it; no where an agent invented it unilaterally. That is a judgement about users, not about code.

DROPPED: MOOT, not answered. Greenfield removes the situation: the loop no longer touches sites anyone asked for, so there is no case in which it might re-publish one. Deleting the question beats deciding it. Recorded rather than erased because the reasoning is what makes the deletion legible.

beads.title: A build concluded 'this build cannot reach poly.pizza' and published it as a general claim
beads.body: True of that run. Wrong as a general claim, and nothing in the system could tell it otherwise because nothing in the system remembered. The agent spent several turns writing an OBJ parser and a file-upload button to work around a fetch failure the harness had already hit and not recorded. THIS BEAD IS THE FIX: a dead-end is read before work starts and is never schedulable.

beads.title: GitHub runs schedule: only from the default branch
beads.body: Three ideas-bot workflows carried a schedule: block and not one ever fired. Every post the account made was a side effect of a push trigger. When the branch merged and the pushes stopped, the posts stopped dead 14 hours before anyone asked why — and the merge made the dead schedules LOOK alive on main. Cadence for anything living off main goes through workers/cron.

beads.title: A squash merge is one commit touching every file the branch ever added
beads.body: Not a merge commit — git diff-tree prints nothing for those, which is why real merges skip safely. A squash is one ordinary single-parent commit, so a path-triggered workflow sees all forty-odd files at once and reruns work weeks late at full agent cost. lab-build.yml carries an explicit merge-day guard for exactly this. Any loop workflow triggered by a path needs the same guard.

beads.title: wrangler deploy does not work from the sandbox — no Cloudflare auth
beads.body: Nor do live PDS/Bluesky writes or remote D1 writes. The deploy workflows ARE the network: to deploy, push to a branch the workflow recognises. Do not spend turns debugging credentials that are not there.

beads.title: Green is not proof: a deploy binds the custom domain or it changed nothing
beads.body: If wrangler.jsonc name is not the worker owning the live custom domain, wrangler deploy updates a stray <name>.workers.dev worker: the run goes green and the live site never changes. Verify by confirming the log binds '<domain> (custom domain)'.

beads.title: Attach loop.mino.mobi as a custom domain (dashboard-only)
beads.body: loop.mino.mobi did not resolve on 2026-08-04, probed from the sandbox with sibling hosts on the same zone answering 200. This is a NEW domain, not an adoption. Attaching one is dashboard-only per DEPLOYS.md 7, so the first deploy-loop run may go green having bound nothing. The route is declared in loop/wrangler.jsonc anyway, which is what makes every later deploy re-bind it. When it is attached and a run has bound it, remove the continue-on-error from the verify step in deploy-loop.yml — otherwise a silent unbinding passes forever.

beads.title: Build the real judge probes: loads, interactive, no console errors, frame budget, keyboard, 380px
beads.body: The probe signal today measures liveness of the LOOP (does the graph lint, did the gate pass), not quality of an ARTIFACT. Naming that distinction is the difference between a judge and a smoke test. These are the artifact probes.

beads.title: wrangler DOES create a new custom domain on deploy — DEPLOYS.md 7 overstates the dashboard-only rule
beads.body: Measured 2026-08-04 on loop.mino.mobi, a hostname that did not resolve before the run. wrangler deploy printed 'Deployed loop triggers / loop.mino.mobi (custom domain)' and the domain came up on its own. DEPLOYS.md 7 lists 'attach / detach custom domains' as dashboard-only; that is right for DETACHING and for moving a domain between workers, but a NEW hostname on a zone already in the account is created by the deploy from the routes[] declaration. Two things follow. First: the first deploy's verify step will still fail, because DNS takes ~10s to resolve and Cloudflare then serves error 1104 for a few minutes while the certificate is issued — attempts 1-2 got NXDOMAIN, 3-5 got 500, and the site answered 200 a few minutes later. Do not diagnose that as a binding failure. Second: the honest check is the wrangler log line, not the curl.

beads.title: DECIDED: the loop runs on a standalone greenfield project, not on community submissions
beads.body: Two reasons, and the second is the larger one. (1) The lab factory's sites are strangers' requests — their projects. An unattended wave of turns is a bad fit for work someone else asked for. (2) THE JUDGE. CLOSED-LOOP 3 is the real blocker: nothing in this repo scores whether a thing is good. On a requested website, better can only be scored by a model against a rubric — the least trustworthy instrument available, needing the most calibration, on work we can least afford to get wrong. Choosing our own target lets us choose a domain with an ORACLE: a score that is not a model's opinion. That converts the hardest unbuilt component into a cheap one. THE COST, stated plainly: the 542-concept pool and the 59 BRIEF.md handoffs were the abundant backlog long-horizon work needs. Greenfield starts with an empty ready queue, and the outbox gate structurally forbids an agent filling it. That is why the planner role becomes necessary rather than optional.

beads.title: Choose the greenfield target — this also settles the coupling shape
beads.body: Greenfield collapses the target choice and CLOSED-LOOP 11.1 into ONE decision. Criteria: an oracle (a score that is not a model's opinion); enough depth that turn 30 has real work; the coupling the estate deliberately lacks; self-contained (no third-party rights, no live data, runs in the sandbox); and able to fail visibly, or it is not an experiment. Recommendation offered and NOT taken: an interpreter and a compiler for one small language, cross-checked by differential testing on generated programs. Operator is describing a different target — pressure-test it against the criteria above and say where it is weak BEFORE committing turns.

beads.title: The planner role: a decomposer that turns a spec into an epic tree
beads.body: Does not exist. The fleet half is built (loop-work); the crew half is not. Greenfield has no inherited backlog, so something must produce one. Needs its own workflow (loop-plan.yml), and it must NOT be the same agent that implements.

beads.title: Generalise the promotion gate from 'not its own work' to 'not a bead it authored'
beads.body: Today loop-apply-outbox.mjs creates every agent proposal as 'proposed', full stop. Correct and too strict for unattended greenfield: nothing would ever become ready without a human at the keyboard. The right rule is that no agent may promote a bead IT AUTHORED — checkable from the actor field the ledger already records, and exactly the crew/fleet split (designer != implementer != reviewer). This is a RELAXATION OF A SAFETY PROPERTY: do not ship it before phase 1 has run human-promoted at least once. Earn it.

beads.title: foam-factorio — production inside the lattice, and the loop's target
beads.body: Sources, processors, defenses and sinks summoned into the voronoi foam as Platonic cells. Stays a puzzle platformer, not a sandbox. Chosen over a compiler, a solver family and a research graph because it is the only candidate that is testable (foam already carries a constructive solvability proof), attractive (strangers click a first-person 3D puzzle; nobody visits a compiler), and deep enough that the agents will genuinely struggle.

beads.title: The summon primitive: Platonic cells from a seed constellation
beads.body: A cell's face normals ARE its neighbour directions, so the constellation is the dual solid's vertices. Exact for all five solids at every aniso tested. verify() is the machine half of the judge for this mechanic: a summon either produced the solid it claimed or it did not, and that is a number.

beads.title: Naive seed constellations are 22 degrees wrong — and the CUBE still looks perfect
beads.body: foam's metric is anisotropic (aniso 2.2), so the bisector normal is M*n, NOT n. Placing neighbours at unit directions times a common radius rotates every off-axis face by 22 degrees. A cube survives because axis-aligned normals are the only ones M cannot rotate — which is the worst outcome, since the cube is what anyone tries first. The wrong conclusion this invites is 'voronoi cells just aren't regular'. They are. n = 2r*Minv*u / (u^T*Minv*u). Do not re-derive this; do not trust a cube as evidence.

beads.title: Math.acos(dot) reports 1.2e-6 degrees of noise for exact unit vectors
beads.body: acos is ill-conditioned near 1: for vectors agreeing to machine precision, dot = 1-eps with eps~2e-16 and acos returns sqrt(2*eps) ~ 2e-8 rad ~ 1.2e-6 degrees. That reads as a real error and invites either 'fixing' exact geometry or widening the tolerance until the check stops catching the 22-degree bug it exists for. Use atan2(|cross|, |dot|) — accurate all the way to zero.

beads.title: A verifier grading against the wrong reference failed correct geometry by exactly the yaw angle
beads.body: constellation() did not return its own rotate parameter, so verify() compared a yawed solid against unrotated normals and reported 36 degrees of error for a 36 degree yaw. A checker that FAILS CORRECT WORK is worse than no checker: it retires a mechanic that was fine, and the retirement looks like evidence.

beads.title: A loop commit under foam/** deploys nothing — deploy-foam is branch-locked
beads.body: deploy-foam.yml triggers only on claude/voronoi-foam-interactive-keo0uy. The loop runs on its own branch, so adding foam/** to the loop's writes wakes NO new workflow — verified with the blast-radius checker. This is the right shape: a human merge is the publication step, so a human decides what strangers see. It is also a hard constraint on feedback latency, and it is why the audience ladder cannot be a per-turn gate.

beads.title: Atomic multi-insert: reformPocket for a whole constellation, all-or-nothing
beads.body: reformPocket(pocket, point) inserts ONE seed and re-derives closure + nav. A half-inserted dodecahedron is not a dodecahedron, so a constellation must land as one transaction with a single closure-and-nav gate at the end — not 13 sequential calls, each of which can refuse. Refusal must roll the whole thing back and say which seed collided.

beads.title: Summon legality as a decidable predicate in a real pocket
beads.body: clearanceNeeded() gives the radius that must be free, but the real test is against a pocket's existing seeds AND the indestructible hull. Make 'can I build here?' answerable BEFORE attempting, so the UI can show buildable space rather than failing on click. Needing clear ground to place a factory is the oldest rule in the genre — the constraint is the mechanic.

beads.title: Object kinds: sources, processors, defenses, sinks as cell roles
beads.body: Which solid means what, what a recipe looks like, and how a role is marked in the render (baseSeedCount already amber-shifts planted chambers — the existing hook). Defenses are the one that may imply an adversary, which would turn the build certificate into a strategy rather than a plan. That is a much larger commitment than the other three — see FACTORIO.md 7.2.

beads.title: Production feasibility oracle — the algebra
beads.body: Sources emit rates, processors transform, sinks demand: a factory is a flow network and satisfiability is a feasibility question over a small non-negative linear system. Exact, cheap, no search, no heuristics. The MARGIN by which a recipe set is satisfiable is also a difficulty dial, the way parMin/parTarget band the walk today.

beads.title: THE BUILD CERTIFICATE — a legal ordering over a self-modifying lattice
beads.body: Prove there exists an ordered sequence of walks and summons such that each summon is legal when attempted, the walker can reach each site GIVEN THE LATTICE AS IT STANDS, and the finished production graph meets demand. The difficulty is that the actions mutate the state space they are searched over: summoning reforms the lattice, so placing an object can open a route, close one, or strand the walker. This is a planning problem over a self-modifying graph — a real CS problem, not a content problem. This is where the turns go.

beads.title: Generation searches build PLANS, not just salts
beads.body: generatePocket retries maxSalt=24 seeds until a walk certificate exists. The factorio generator must retry until a PLAN exists, and that search is orders of magnitude larger. Keep the invariant that no unproven pocket is ever returned.

beads.title: Par and the difficulty band generalise to build cost
beads.body: Par counts breaches today. It becomes a cost over breaches + summons + distance, and the puzzle band moves with it. Without this there is no difficulty oracle for factory levels and 'par in band' stops meaning anything.

beads.title: Per-turn frame-budget number under N summons on mobile
beads.body: A dodecahedron is 13 seeds; ten is +130 against a base pocket of ~294, and buildComplex runs on every summon while mobile performance is a hard requirement. Rich factories and the frame budget pull against each other. Turn this from a discipline into a NUMBER the judge reads, or gate 7 does not exist.

beads.title: PHASE 0 — will strangers actually vote? Ship the pairwise page against hand-made variants
beads.body: The ladder needs N. If foam draws five visitors a week it never resolves and the programme stalls on a distribution problem wearing an engineering costume. Ship the A/B comparison against two HAND-MADE variants and count votes. Randomise order, record it, and check the control: if position predicts preference better than version does, the signal is noise. A negative result here ends the programme for zero model spend — which is the best kind of phase, and the reason this is P0.

beads.title: How do strangers vote, and where is it stored?
beads.body: OPERATOR'S CALL. atpolls-db exists with 8 dependents and poll/ already does anonymous voting properly. Reusing it buys infrastructure and buys blast radius. Deliberate coupling is wanted (CLOSED-LOOP 11.1); accidental coupling is not.

beads.title: Replace the judge's 'rubric' signal with human pairwise preference?
beads.body: OPERATOR'S CALL, and there is a KNOWN INCONSISTENCY until it is made: FACTORIO.md 5 argues the quality signal should be pairwise preference between consecutive turns' output, while .github/loop/config.json still lists signals [probes, rubric, adversarial]. The config was left alone deliberately rather than edited to match the prose — it is the live control surface and this is a design decision, not a typo. The argument for the swap: the programme's question is 'does turn 20 beat turn 19', and a pairwise A/B asks exactly that, with no rubric to write and no calibration to do. The argument against: pairwise needs traffic (see the phase 0 bead) and settles over days rather than per turn, so it cannot be a per-turn gate. Resolve this before enabling the loop, or the config and the design record disagree in public.

beads.title: AUDIT: the ready queue held zero class-A requirements — it looked healthy and was starved
beads.body: Applied the Definition of Ready to the eight beads sitting in the queue an hour after authoring them. Two were PHASES pretending to be tickets (fail R1 one-turn and R2 names-its-gate). Three were class B — they BUILD gates, so they define what done means and an agent must not self-serve them. Two were human-only infrastructure with no machine gate. One was already finished and nobody had closed it. Net class-A count available to an unattended fleet: ZERO. The queue length said eight. This is the exact failure the WBS names: starved and idle look identical from outside, and a rich backlog with no schedulable work is a stalled programme reading as a healthy one. Count class A, not beads.

beads.title: The promotion rule is the loop's GAIN control — it is why nothing has run away yet
beads.body: The chain grows by BRANCHING FACTOR, not by speed. Gain = expected successor turns per turn: below 1 it dies out, at 1 it is self-sustaining forever, above 1 it is exponential. Today gain is structurally ZERO for anything the fleet produces, because loop-apply-outbox.mjs creates every agent proposal as 'proposed' and never 'ready' — the loop drains what a human put in the queue and halts. That rule was written as a quality gate; it turns out to be the strongest regulator in the system. WBS phase 3.2, relaxing it to 'not a bead it authored', is EXACTLY the change that lifts gain off zero. It must not ship unless something else holds gain below one.

beads.title: A rate limit is a saturation, not a regulator — and running at it destroys the measurement
beads.body: Using the account's usage limit as the governor fails twice. Informationally: pinned at the ceiling, utilisation reads 100% whether the loop is producing or spinning, so throughput becomes a property of the limit rather than of the work — and this programme exists to measure whether the work keeps paying. Practically: the limit is shared with the operator, so a regulator whose set-point is 'all of it' collides rather than regulates. The honest version is a HEADROOM RESERVE: target a fraction, observe consumption, back off when the operator is active.

beads.title: Adopt the three-mechanism regulator: enabled / spend bucket / lease?
beads.body: OPERATOR'S CALL. Three mechanisms answering three different questions — may it run at all (enabled, built), how fast (a token bucket denominated in SPEND rather than turns, refilled on a clock), and until when (a lease with an expiry that the reactor refuses to dispatch past). The lease is the one that matters for unattended running: counters miscount across restarts, are ambiguous under parallelism, and — fatally — NEGLECT LETS THEM CONTINUE. A lease fails closed, and it expresses 'let it run tonight' directly, which is the actual posture. Adopting this deprecates turnsPerDay.

beads.title: Per-turn spend accounting: make cost an observable, not an assumption
beads.body: claude -p --max-budget-usd bounds one turn; nothing accumulates it. Without accumulation there is no bucket, no headroom reserve and no honest cost curve — and CLOSED-LOOP 10's estimate stays the weakest number in the programme. The turn record in runs.jsonl already has a slot for it.

beads.title: The clock half of the hybrid: cron-driven refill so the chain cannot self-sustain
beads.body: The chain is built; the clock is not. Hybrid: the chain may continue while tokens remain, and when the bucket empties it stops and waits for the clock to refill. Burst latency when there is budget, externally-bounded rate when there is not. Depends on CRON_GITHUB_PAT, which has never been set — workers/cron has dispatched nothing in its entire life.
